note:
Researched from live web sources in a Claude Code session — no paid API, no key, no cost.

`case` is the argument for picking them; `watch_out` is the honest counter-argument, because a recommendation you can't argue against isn't advice. `key_stats` holds the hard numbers as discrete facts. `voices` records what named outlets actually said — 'analysts say' is not a source. `dissent` marks a genuine split.

WRITTEN 31 AUGUST, four days before the Gameweek 3 deadline (18:30 BST, Friday 4 September). That timing is recorded honestly throughout rather than hidden: the Friday press conferences have NOT happened, Fantasy Football Scout's Gameweek 3 Scout Picks are an early draft the site says it will revise, no Gameweek 3 captaincy poll or clean-sheet odds have been published yet, and the summer transfer window does not close until 1 September. Anything depending on those is labelled `unconfirmed` rather than dressed up as settled. THIS FILE SHOULD BE REFRESHED AGAIN ON DEADLINE DAY.

Three things shape the week and none of them is a projection:
  1. Manchester City host Coventry. Every source that has published on Gameweek 3 leads with it, and the question being asked is not "captain Haaland?" but "Triple Captain Haaland?".
  2. The transfer window shuts on 1 September, three days before the deadline. Enzo Fernández is unresolved and Omar Marmoush has just arrived at Spurs. A squad decision taken now can be overtaken by a Monday-night announcement.
  3. The market has piled into the cheap Newcastle assets — Wissa, Elanga, Hall — while Scout point out that Isak, the premium in the same team with the same fixture, is on 16.2% ownership and outside the top twenty transfers in.

One entry, De Cuyper, is tiered `neutral` and says plainly that no verified source covered him for Gameweek 3. That is a gap being reported as a gap. It is not the same thing as an assessment, and it must not be read as one.

Club-wide verdicts do NOT belong here; they live in teams.json.

players.name: Haaland
players.verdict: Home to a promoted side, four days after a brace, in the week the chip conversation opens. There is no argument on the other side of this one.
players.case: Manchester City host Coventry City, and Fantasy Football Scout's early Scout Picks are built around that one fixture — the piece is literally titled 'Piling up on Man City'. Their framing of the armband is not whether Haaland is the captain but whether this is the week to Triple Captain him. The supporting number they use is blunt: only Palace and Spurs sit below Coventry for goal difference and points. He also comes into it having scored twice in Gameweek 2 off five attempts while, in Scout's own words, barely touching the ball — which is the version of Haaland that wins gameweeks, because it means the blank risk is not a performance risk, it is a variance risk. He was heavily sold after the Gameweek 1 blank. Those managers have now paid for it twice.
players.watch_out: The only real question is chip timing, not selection. If you fire the Triple Captain here you cannot fire it at a double gameweek later, and City have played two competitive games and conceded in both, so the match could be more open than a home tie with a promoted side suggests. There is also a genuine pattern worth naming: Scout's own Gameweek 2 notes had him scoring twice from five shots having 'barely touched the ball', which is a polite way of saying City are not funnelling everything through him under Maresca the way they did under Guardiola. Foden topped the expected-goal-involvement table that week, not Haaland.

players.name: Cherki
players.verdict: The most clearly argued buy of the week — and the one place where the sources openly contradict each other about whether he is actually any good.
players.case: Four attacking returns in two matches, including two solo goals at Selhurst Park on Friday, and an underlying rate that Scout summarises as a chance created every sixteen minutes. All About FPL put the same case in different numbers: four goal involvements, two assists and 0.86 xA, plus the bonus-point behaviour they look for in a midfielder. At £7.6m he is the cheap route into the Coventry fixture, and Scout name him and Foden as the two City players managers are weighing to complete a triple-up alongside Haaland.
players.watch_out: Two separate warnings, both from the same site that recommends him. First, the fixtures immediately turn: Scout point out he faces Manchester United and Liverpool away in the three gameweeks that follow, so this is a buy with a short runway unless you are happy holding through that. Second, and more awkwardly, their Gameweek 2 notes ran under the headline calling his first-half display 's**t' — he was quiet before the interval and, in their words, did not sound far from being substituted at half-time. He also did not start Gameweek 1. The second-half masterclass is real; so is the fact that he has been a second-half player.

players.name: Foden
players.verdict: Topped the expected-goal-involvement table in Gameweek 2 and finished with two assists rather than the hat-trick the chances deserved. At £7.0m that gap is the buy.
players.case: Scout's Gameweek 2 notes have him top of the whole game's xGI table, with two assists — one for Cherki, one for Haaland. He is named alongside Cherki as the cheaper Manchester City option managers are considering to complete a triple-up for the Coventry fixture, and at £7.0m he is the same price as Szoboszlai and Marmoush for a starting place in the best attack in the division.
players.watch_out: The reason he only has assists is the same reason to be careful: Scout describe him being 'too hesitant to pounce on a loose ball', skying a close-range effort and miscuing a header from four yards. Two big chances missed in one match. Operating from the right wing he is getting into the positions, but the finishing has not followed, and Manchester City have enough attacking options that a bad run costs minutes.

players.name: Isak
players.verdict: Scout's phrase, not mine: the cheat code this week. Premium forward numbers, the best attacking fixture on the board, and almost nobody buying him.
players.case: Fantasy Football Scout say he has all the underlying numbers you want from a premium forward and now gets arguably the best possible fixture for an attacking asset, at home to Bournemouth. The part that makes him interesting rather than merely good is the ownership: 16.2% selected, and he is not in the top twenty most-transferred-in players this gameweek. Everyone is buying Wissa, Elanga and Hall — the Newcastle players around him — and skipping the forward. Newcastle also have what Scout call a great run of fixtures until Gameweek 10 with no European football, so this is not a one-week punt.
players.watch_out: Newcastle have not won any of their last eight league meetings with Bournemouth. That is a real record against exactly the fixture the case rests on, and it is the reason the crowd is buying the £5-6m Newcastle players instead of the premium. He is also expensive, so owning him and Haaland together squeezes the rest of the squad.

players.name: Szoboszlai
players.verdict: Being sold in volume by managers who did not look at what he actually did. Two sources independently say hold, and the fixture is Ipswich away.
players.case: All About FPL point out he has the second-highest FPL points total and the second-highest xGI of any Liverpool player, and is nonetheless one of the most transferred-out players in the game — against Ipswich, who conceded five in their last match. Scout add the detail that explains the apparent blank: he had no attacking return in Gameweek 2 but banked defensive contribution points, because a shift to right-back helped him clear the DefCon threshold. That is the classic hold — the scoring route changed, the scoring did not stop. He also took every set piece for Liverpool in Gameweek 1, and scored a late penalty to rescue a draw, so he is on spot kicks in a Salah-less side.
players.watch_out: The deeper and now wider role is the counter-argument and it is a fair one: a midfielder playing at right-back is scoring 2-point DefCon returns rather than goals and assists, and DefCon points have a hard ceiling. If Iraola keeps using him there, the £7.0m is buying a floor rather than a ceiling. Liverpool also remain short in attack — Ekitike is out with an Achilles injury and Scout note Salah has not been truly replaced — so the chances he is feeding may not be finished.

players.name: Enzo
players.verdict: Unresolved four days before the deadline, and the window shuts three days before it. Do not carry an unresolved transfer saga into a gameweek you cannot change.
players.case: The case for holding is narrower than it was but it exists. Sky Sports reported Manchester City missed Chelsea's 5pm Friday deadline without bidding, and that Chelsea now expect Fernández to be with them for the entire 2026/27 season. Fantasy Football Scout's early predicted line-up for the Arsenal fixture has him starting in the 4-2-3-1 behind João Pedro, which is the first positive minutes evidence he has had this season. Chelsea are also depleted — Cucurella, Gittens and Estêvão are all out with hamstring injuries and Fofana is suspended — which argues for using the senior players available.
players.watch_out: Everything else. The reporting has not settled: Sky Sports also report City remain interested despite missing the deadline and will decide before the window closes on 1 September, and that Chelsea are prepared to sell at the right price against a £120m valuation. GOAL report he has verbally agreed personal terms with City. Sports Mole report City expect to finalise the deal despite a price hike. Football365 report a formal bid and City accelerating 'in the next few days', with the move said to depend on whether Rodri leaves for Barcelona. He came off the bench rather than starting the opener and was then left out of a Carabao Cup squad entirely. A predicted line-up published on 31 August cannot know what happens on 1 September.
